fields.body: The shape of the engagement follows the problem. The solution may be advice, a focused build, training, ongoing execution, or a combination.

steps.title: The session
steps.body: We learn how the business works, what the team wants to change, and where time or revenue is being lost.

steps.title: The plan
steps.body: A written recommendation: where AI fits, the right type of solution, what should happen first, and why.

steps.title: The delivery
steps.body: We provide the agreed consulting, custom build, integrations, training, or managed execution against a clear scope.

steps.title: The improvement
steps.body: When ongoing help makes sense, we run the work, support the team, measure what changes, and keep improving it.

fields.heading: You leave the first session with a written plan.
fields.body: Thirty minutes. You describe how the business runs and what you want to change. We identify where AI or automation fits, recommend the right kind of solution, and put the next steps in writing. Yours to keep either way.
items: Where AI or automation is genuinely useful
Whether the answer is advice, a workflow, an agent, an integration, training, or execution
What should happen first and why
The tools, access, people, and approvals the work needs
A clear scope, ownership model, and way to measure progress

fields.yearsLabel: Years deploying machine learning at scale
fields.body: We put AI into production long before the hype cycle. Knowing exactly where to deploy automation, and what will break when you do, is the difference between a system that runs and one that needs babysitting.
fields.detail: We are deliberately selective. You interface directly with the engineers architecting your system, never an account manager. The practice is led by John Connor.

fields.title: Answered plainly.
questions: How soon would we see a result?
Nobody here is technical. Is that a problem?
Our data is disorganized. Fix that first?
We bought an AI tool and nobody uses it.
answers: The session and the plan cost nothing. Delivery is a fixed price agreed before work begins. If a project is too small to justify the fee, we will say so on the session.
It depends on the recommendation. A training or workflow engagement can move quickly; a custom build or broader execution scope takes longer. We define the first useful result before work begins.
No, and it is the usual case. You explain how the business runs. We handle the rest, and your team is trained on anything they touch.
No. Waiting to clean it up is the most common reason projects never start. We scope around what exists and improve the rest along the way.
Common. Sometimes the right answer is training, clearer rules, or a better workflow around the tool rather than another purchase. We recommend that when it is the smallest useful fix.
It stays in your accounts. We use providers with no-training agreements, give each system access only to what it needs, and log what it touches. Bring your compliance requirements to the first call.
You do. The accounts, the code, the documentation. Support is available and optional, and nothing is built so that you need us to keep it running.

props.text: Spend development effort on your business's own process

Reuse customer identity, conversations, opportunities, tasks, access and business services. Build an industry report, specialized workspace or custom lifecycle, then make supported operations available to AI through the shared tools.
Own the installation and handoff

The application source is MIT licensed. A connected installation uses your own Supabase project and provider accounts, with hosting and usage costs. Current custom App development uses the source and an external coding agent. General-purpose App creation inside the workspace remains planned.

metadata.title: Compare Command Center and alternatives
metadata.description: Choose between a CRM, business suite, app builder and an adaptable business platform.

props.heading: Choose the platform around the work you need.
props.body: Official product descriptions reviewed 2026-10-10. This guide explains strengths and fit; it does not certify feature parity or quoted pricing.

props.text: Twenty

Customizable CRM. Twenty leads with an open-source CRM that technical teams can adapt, including custom data, interfaces and automation.

Consider it when a customizable CRM is the main system you need.

Consider Command Center when you want to start from customer work spanning sales, delivery, invoicing and publishing, and extend that operating foundation.
Kyma / Mila Omni

AI application creation. Kyma's public documentation describes generating React applications, working with drafts, previewing changes and publishing workstations.

Evaluate it when creating applications from prompts inside the product is central to your requirements. Validate the described workflow with your own trial.

Command Center's custom App path currently uses the source repository and an external coding agent. Choose it for the existing business services you can reuse; its general-purpose in-app App builder remains planned.
Attio

Revenue CRM. Attio organizes its AI CRM around building pipeline, converting leads, running sales motions, forecasting and account growth.

Consider it when your principal goal is a focused sales and revenue CRM.

Consider Command Center when customer operations also need delivery tasks, billing, content and custom Apps in a source-owned platform.
HubSpot

Customer platform. HubSpot presents a shared CRM across marketing, sales, service, content, data and commerce, with connected AI capabilities.

Consider it when you want an established hosted customer platform and its packaged ecosystem.

Consider Command Center when controlling the application source and adapting domain workflows matter enough to take on a configured implementation.
HighLevel

Agency and marketing operations. HighLevel connects lead capture, nurture, closing and reactivation, with agency-oriented accounts, marketing channels and AI features.

Consider it when packaged agency marketing and customer-acquisition workflows are your primary requirement.

Consider Command Center when your agency wants to build client-specific operational Apps from an MIT-licensed foundation. Check each required channel against the current connection guides.
Zoho One

Integrated business suite. Zoho One combines business applications with AI, integrations, automation and custom application development.

Consider it when broad packaged application coverage is more useful than maintaining your own platform source.

Consider Command Center when shared customer operations and your own business-specific extensions are the starting point. Compare the actual workflows you need rather than the size of the app catalog.
Odoo / ERPNext

ERP and broad operations. Odoo and ERPNext cover broad business operations, including accounting, sales, purchasing, inventory and projects.

Consider them when a full ERP, stock management, manufacturing or accounting ledger is central to the project.

Command Center currently focuses on customer work, delivery, billing and adaptable Apps. Evaluate its current guides for those jobs and scope additional ERP functions separately.
Retool / n8n

Apps and workflow automation. Retool provides applications, workflows and agents around business data. n8n provides composable automation and AI workflows across connected systems.

Consider them when you primarily need to build tools or orchestrate systems you already use.

Consider Command Center when you also want existing customer, opportunity, task and billing workflows to build on. Custom integrations still need their own implementation and verification.
